text.p: Motorola Inc said Friday it started shipping its 300-MHz volume desktop and portable microprocessor.
The company said the higher speed microprocessors allow manufacturers to build systems ranging from subnotebooks and laptops to high-performance notebook and desktop systems.
Motorola said it has exceeded its previously-stated goal of reaching 300 MHz on PowerPC 603e microprocessors by the end of 1997.
RISC-based PowerPC chips are developed jointly by Motorola, IBM Corp and Apple Computer Inc.
In a separate release, Apple said it would ship its newest mainstream computers, the Power Macintosh 6500 series, based on the 225-MHz and 300-MHz Motorola chips.
Motorola's new chip is priced at $618 when purchased in quantities of 1,000 and is immediately available, the company said.
